correctness.rationale: For c(n)=floor(n^2/4)/n the exact parity formulas imply strict monotonicity; c(13)=42/13>3 restricts every entry to 2..12, while c(2)=1/2 bounds the multiset cardinality by six. This proves a finite complete search domain; an independently written exact-rational nondecreasing tuple enumeration found exactly 78 feasible multisets, whose unique largest lcm is 60 at (3,4,5), with cost 43/15. This is an exhaustive finite proof after the cutoff, unlike mere sampling. An I_n fiber component group is Z/n, and the exponent of a product is the lcm. The geometric statement is only a conditional inequality and correctly avoids asserting an existing surface with the extremal data.

value.rationale: The exponent of the product of reducible Kodaira I_n component groups is a canonical natural integer invariant of semistable elliptic fibrations, and chi=3 is the first Kodaira-dimension-one Euler-characteristic value. A complete sharp numerical bound and equality classification under the geometric polyhedrality criterion is a useful finite boundary datum; it does not overstate physical geometric attainability or apply to Mordell–Weil torsion itself.

final_claim: Every nonempty finite multiset of integers n_i>=2 with sum floor(n_i^2/4)/n_i<=3 has lcm(n_i)<=60, equality exactly for multiset {3,4,5}. Hence the product of the cyclic component groups attached to any corresponding semistable Jacobian elliptic surface with chi=3, finite MW and polyhedrality condition has exponent <=60; geometric realization of {3,4,5} is NOT asserted.
